sections.review: Linux syscall declarations and conditional completion emission, errno mapping, poll/reactor bounded stack and source layout, x64 IPv4/IPv6 endpoint network byte order.
CLOEXEC socket creation/accept, reverse error cleanup, bounded scalar/range and64-element vectored IO, msghdr/iovec layout and per-buffer receive length distribution, shutdown/socket options.
Linger rounding and disabled sentinel, timeval overflow and rounding checks, UDP MSG_TRUNC/clamp and address publication, endpoint queries, reactor waiter eventfd/epoll setup.

Cancellation/status release-acquire publication, tagged registration identity, direction and readiness masks, terminal task wake/unregister races, bounded reactor allocations and reverse failure cleanup, registration/remove ownership.

Submit association and rearm, immediate vs pending error paths, cancel wake and terminal arbitration, dequeue claim and exact buffer transfer, pending cancellation drain followed by waiter stop/join and single owner cleanup.

findings.source: Ordinary send669 uses16384; completion waiter1571 and submit2106 use0. Need verify whether closed-peer completion sends can terminate with SIGPIPE under actual emitted program signal policy.
findings.next: Check shared program signal setup; CSharp extracted production immediate/waiter send controls with peer-close and ordinary send control before any compiler edit.

findings.source: Waiter1551..1555 tests only direction ready bit before issuing; an event containing only error/hangup goes to rearm, not terminal syscall/error decoding.
findings.next: CSharp controlled epoll error-only/hangup-only event reproduction and normal direction controls; do not conclude from source alone.

findings.source: Submit duplicate check tests application key only, not registration. Waiter branches from first matching pending registration into issue/rearm; epoll interest is direction-specific perregistration.
